dek: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade steps off Nov 26 with a record 100 inflatables.

slides.label: The Basics
slides.text: Thursday, Nov. 26, *8:30 a.m.*, 2.5 miles from the Upper West Side to Herald Square. Free to watch.

slides.label: Watch It
slides.text: Catch it live on *NBC and Peacock*, Telemundo's Spanish simulcast, encore at 2 p.m. ET/PT.

slides.label: Lineup
slides.text: *Megan Moroney* and *Teddy Swims* headline Herald Square, plus Feid, Queen Latifah, Wyclef Jean and more.

slides.label: New Balloons
slides.text: 100 inflatables means first flights for *Bluey*, *Hello Kitty*, and Underdog's return since 1984.

slides.label: Throwbacks
slides.text: *Felix the Cat*, the parade's first balloon from 1927, and the long lost *Blue Hippopotamus* fly again.

slides.label: Where to Stand
slides.text: Central Park West from *75th to 61st*, arrive by 6 a.m. Sixth Avenue draws the bigger crowds.

slides.label: Inflation Night
slides.text: Wednesday, Nov. 25: queue opens noon, viewing starts *1 p.m.*, line closes *6 p.m.* at 72nd and Columbus.

slides.label: Getting There
slides.text: Subway runs a *Sunday schedule*, some stops close 4 to 11 a.m. Leave the car home, streets shut down.

caption_instagram:
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026 marks 100 years with a record 100 inflatables floating over Manhattan on Nov. 26.

Felix the Cat, the parade's first balloon back in 1927, returns. So does the Blue Hippopotamus, the one balloon Macy's never recovered after it drifted away in 1931. New flyers like Bluey, Hello Kitty and a reimagined Underdog join the sky, while Megan Moroney and Teddy Swims headline Herald Square.

Want the best spot? Central Park West from 75th to 61st gets you there by 6 a.m. Balloon inflation on Wednesday, Nov. 25 opens at noon on the Upper West Side, and once that line closes at 6 p.m., you're done.

caption_linkedin:
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade turns 100 this year, and the production behind it is a masterclass in scale.

A record 100 inflatables over Manhattan. More than 11,000 volunteers and participants marching. A 2.5 mile route planned down to the inch, with staging areas expanding onto West 72nd Street for the centennial. Security considerations shifting entire viewing blocks. A balloon inflation line with a hard stop at 6 p.m., no exceptions.

Behind every float and float sponsor, from DoorDash to HBO to Planters, is a brand betting on one morning of live national attention on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo.

For founders and operators, the parade is a reminder that legacy and logistics move together. A hundred years doesn't run itself. It runs on planning, partnerships and showing up on time, every single year.
